Good morning, and thank you for joining us. This morning, Northway Group announced an agreement to acquire Brightline Logistics. The deal is valued at one point two billion dollars and is expected to close in the first quarter of next year, subject to regulatory approval. It is estimated that the combined company will save around forty million dollars a year by the end of year two. Brightline's brand will remain, and Mark Ellison is expected to stay as president. We know there is a lot of speculation about job cuts. I can tell you that there are no plans to close any Brightline office this year. We will not comment on rumors about other buyers. I'll now take a few questions.

In business news this morning, Northway Group is buying Brightline Logistics in a deal worth one point two billion dollars. Analysts say the price is fair. The deal is expected to be accretive in its first full year, which means Northway's earnings per share should go up. Shareholders seemed to agree: Northway stock rose four percent in early trading. However, the deal still needs regulatory approval in two countries, and that could take six months. Other buyers are believed to have looked at Brightline last year, but nobody made a formal offer. Brightline's chief executive, Mark Ellison, is said to be staying. We will have more on this story at noon.
